extracted.intended_audience: participants in U.S. antidumping/countervailing investigations and administrative reviews (exporters, producers, importers, petitioners, counsel, and Customs officials)
extracted.subtask_description: Department of Commerce procedural and substantive standards for calculating U.S. price, foreign market value/constructed value, expense allocations, and evidentiary/showing requirements in antidumping and countervailing duty investigations and administrative reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign currency conversion rule
rubrics_metrics.description: All conversions of foreign currency into U.S. currency be made at the rate in effect on the date of sale (19 CFR 353.60 (1989); section 773(a)(1) of the Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If charges (e.g., ocean freight, marine insurance) were incurred in foreign currency, convert using the exchange rate in effect on the date the charge was incurred/sale date as required by regulation; review invoices at verification to confirm currency incurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessory vs. integral part classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether an item assigned to a sale is within the scope of the investigation or is an accessory and not an 'integral' part of the basic machine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an item is an accessory with an identifiable and segregable price, exclude its price and manufacturing cost from the model/transaction price (MTP) and cost of manufacture (COM). See DOC Position to Comment 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising expenses treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertising expenses directed to end-users are properly claimed as indirect selling expenses and are not deducted from U.S. price for purchase price transactions (19 CFR 353.56(a)(2) (1989)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify whether advertising was directed to end-users on the respondent's behalf and whether negotiations/sales were between end-user and respondent; if so, treat advertising as indirect selling expense and do not deduct from U.S. price for purchase price transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product liability insurance premium allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Product liability insurance premiums that cover all sales worldwide and are not solely and directly applicable to subject merchandise should be treated as indirect selling or general and administrative expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the policy covers all sales regardless of product or market and premiums are fixed and not incurred with each sale, treat as indirect selling/G&A. Verify absence of reserves for settlements or litigation during the POI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation requirement for sales through trading companies
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must explain transaction process for sales to trading companies (who invoiced whom, invoice amounts) and provide invoices/payment documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If respondent provides invoices and verification documentation showing sales were to trading companies and no commissions were paid, no adjustment; if information is missing, Department may use best information available (BIA) and deduct portion of sales value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of U.S. indirect selling expenses in constructed value (CV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Home market selling expenses are appropriate for use in constructed value; U.S. indirect selling expenses are relevant only in analyzing export sales price (ESP) transactions, not purchase price transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In accordance with section 773(e)(1)(B) of the Act, use the respondent’s verified home market indirect selling expenses when calculating general expenses for CV, even if no 'similar' merchandise sales occurred, provided same general class or kind of merchandise is claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profit in constructed value: statutory minimum
rubrics_metrics.description: If profit earned on home market sales is less than the statutory minimum, use the statutory minimum of eight percent for profit in CV calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify profit on similar-sized and all home market MTPs; if all profits are below statutory minimum, apply statutory minimum (8%) in CV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of package processing costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Processing costs accumulated in a separate job order for a package sale should be allocated to each piece of equipment based on identifiable cost drivers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If respondent cannot specifically identify costs per piece, allocate based on cost of manufacture (COM) when verification evidence (e.g., work reports) indicates greater work was performed on more expensive pieces; equal allocation only if supported by records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation of related-party purchases
rubrics_metrics.description: For constructed value, use transfer prices between related companies unless such prices do not fairly reflect market prices in the market under consideration (section 773(e)(2) of the Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If transfer prices cannot be tested against market prices (e.g., fully integrated producers, custom products) and transfer prices are below cost of production (COP), use COP as representative of fair market prices. Consider corporate integration and exclusive sales to the parent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of scrap costs and inventory write-downs
rubrics_metrics.description: Scrap costs charged to 'Loss on Sale of Inventories and Write-down of Inventories' that are not project-specific should be treated as manufacturing costs and allocated over all production based on COM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If scrapped parts are not attributed to particular units, allocate over total production using COM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest expense offset
rubrics_metrics.description: Interest expense may be offset with interest income if the offset claim is timely and the interest income is related to production operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm at verification that offset claim was made timely and that interest income included in offset relates solely to production/operations before allowing offset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of liquidation and cash deposit instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Customs shall continue to suspend liquidation and require cash deposit or posting of bond equal to the estimated amounts by which foreign market value exceeds U.S. price (section 733(d) of the Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct Customs to require deposit equal to estimated dumping margin for entries on or after publication date; suspension remains until further notice or final order. If ITC finds no injury, refund/cancel securities.

rubrics_metrics.name: United States price calculation (purchase price method)
rubrics_metrics.description: United States price is calculated using purchase price as defined in section 772 of the Tariff Act, typically based on FOB port price to unrelated purchasers with appropriate deductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make deductions for foreign inland freight and brokerage/handling. Use market-economy data for deductions where available; where not available, use surrogate or best information available (e.g., charges incurred in surrogate country).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign market value approach for state-controlled economies
rubrics_metrics.description: When a country is a state-controlled economy, use prices or constructed value of such or similar merchandise sold by countries whose economy is not state-controlled, or value factors of production in a comparable economy (pre-1988 section 773(c) and 19 CFR 353.8 (1988)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for determining FMV based on sales prices in a comparable non-state-controlled economy at a similar stage of development; if sales data unavailable, use factors-of-production method and surrogate valuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of surrogate country and data
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose surrogate country(ies) comparable in stage of economic development and able to provide complete, publicly available data for valuation of factors of production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple comparable countries exist, prefer those with verifiable, complete public data (here, Portugal was selected because of more complete data). Do not use responses that raise propriety/relationship concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of market-economy supplier prices where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Value factors of production on the basis of prices paid by the respondent to market-economy suppliers when such prices are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When market-economy prices are not provided, obtain values from public sources in the surrogate country (e.g., embassy data, BLS, OECD indicators) and adjust for inflation to represent the POI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material cost calculation method
rubrics_metrics.description: Material costs for components (e.g., steel) are calculated by multiplying gross weight by unit price less scrap value; scrap factor adjusted to reflect only the portion considered salable, with waste included in cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not add scrap value to net value; ensure scrap/waste are correctly categorized and included in cost where appropriate; verify respondent's identification of waste and calculation methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of embassy and official statistics for factor valuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use data from sources such as American Embassy reports, U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, and OECD Main Economic Indicators to value labor, scrap, factory overhead, inland freight, and to adjust for inflation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the surrogate country's embassy provides values (e.g., for skilled/unskilled labor, overhead), use them; if embassy lacks certain data (e.g., trained labor), use BLS or other reliable sources; adjust values to the review period using OECD indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory minima for general expenses and profit in CV
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply statutory minima where appropriate: use ten percent of the sum of material and fabrication costs for general expenses and eight percent of material and fabrication costs plus general expenses for profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these minima when calculating constructed value if applicable and consistent with statute and prior practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packing value sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Value for packing may be based on market-economy data from prior public case records (e.g., packing values used in Antifriction Bearings public file), adjusted to the period of review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comparable prior case packing values tied to the surrogate country and adjust for the review period with appropriate inflation indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of respondent's reported factors of production
rubrics_metrics.description: When using factors-of-production methodology, calculate constructed value based on the factors of production reported by the respondent, subject to necessary adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make adjustments where respondent data are incomplete or inconsistent and supplement with surrogate/public data as needed; verify reported factors at verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment and hearing procedure for administrative reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Case briefs and written comments (ten copies) must be submitted by specified deadlines; rebuttal briefs by a later deadline; Department will hold a public hearing, if requested, and allow affirmative oral presentations only on arguments included in briefs (19 CFR 353.38).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing requests must be submitted within ten days of publication and include: party’s name, address, telephone number; reasons for attending; list of issues to be discussed; and number of participants. Only issues raised in briefs may be presented orally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of best information available (BIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: If respondent fails to provide requested information (e.g., commission amounts, invoice details), the Department may use the best information available to make deductions or adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use BIA sparingly and after verification efforts; when documentation is provided and verified, do not apply adverse BIA adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash deposit rate instructions post-review
rubrics_metrics.description: Cash deposit rate for a producer/exporter will be that established in the final results of the administrative review and will be effective upon publication of final results of that review (section 751(a)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This deposit requirement applies to shipments entered on or after the publication date of the final results and remains in effect until the final results of the next administrative review are published.
